claims.text: The Rendlesham record is an unavoidable counter-example to Condign's denial of any UK-US collaboration on the topic, because the incident occurred at a US-operated base in the UK Air Defence Region and generated documents held on both sides. Reasoning: the physical facts of the case require at minimum that the two governments held overlapping records, whatever the DI55 staff's own access was.

connections.note: The National Archives itself billed the tranche as containing 'Britain's very own Roswell - Rendlesham Forest in Suffolk'.

desc: The Rendlesham Forest incident of December 1980 - the events at RAF Woodbridge and RAF Bentwaters in Suffolk, then hosting United States Air Force units, that produced the Halt memorandum and the Halt tape - is the single case that dominates British UAP discussion, and The National Archives' own framing of the August 2009 tranche put it front and centre: the files, covering 1981 to 1996, invited the public to 'find out more about close encounters, stray satellites, bright lights and Britain's very own Roswell - Rendlesham Forest in Suffolk'. That tranche comprised DEFE 24/1948/1, DEFE 24/1959/1 to 1965/1, DEFE 24/1970/1 to 1976/1 and DEFE 24/2086/1. Rendlesham is the point at which the British and American records are physically the same record: the deputy base commander who wrote the memorandum was a United States Air Force officer, the base was a US-operated facility on British soil, and the MoD's own handling of the case sits inside DEFE 24. The case therefore sits directly across the sentence in Project Condign Volume 3 asserting that there is 'no intelligence exchange or access or collaboration of any sort' between the UK and the USA on the topic.
